Inclusion criteria: 
Infants born with postmenstrual age less than 28 weeks
Signed informed consent, unless the NICU has chosen to use 'opt-out' or deferred consent as a consent method.

Exclusion criteria: 
Missing written parental informed consent (if the 'opt-out' method is used for consent, lack of a record that the clinical staff have explained the trial and the 'opt-out' consent process to parents and/or a record in the infant's clinical file of parents' decision to opt-out, are exclusion criteria)
Decision not to conduct full life support
No possibility to place cerebral NIRS oximeter within six hours after birth

Group differences: The characteristics of the infants were similar in the two groups

Total sample size: 1601

Withdrawals:  13 in NIRS group;  9 in NO NIRS group
Reasons for withdrawal: 

Mainly because of withdrawn informed consent.

The parents of 18 infants who were enroled under the terms of deferred consent did not eventually provide written informed consent and declined the use of their infants’ data. For three infants who were enroled under the terms of prior informed consent, the parents withdrew their consent and, for two of the three infants, also withdrew consent for the use of their infants’ data. Two infants from one site were lost to follow-up because the site withdrew from the trial shortly after the start of data collection.

Other: Serious adverse reactions included severe skin damage, physical injury associated with managing the device and sensors (critical displacement of endotracheal tubes or endovascular lines caused by cerebral oximetry monitoring), and clinical mismanagement (i.e., interventions aimed at improving respiratory or cardiovascular status and oxygen transport) that occurred on the basis of oximetry monitoring

Neonates born more than 8 weeks preterm (gestational age up to 31 weeks and 6 days); decision to conduct full life support; parental informed consent; and cerebral NIRS oximeter placed within three minutes after birth.


Exclusion criteria:
